data.name: Ayudhja
data.gender_notes: Ayudhja is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'ayudh', meaning 'weapon' or 'armor'. The name Ayudhja carries the meaning “Weapon or Armor” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ayudhja usually hope their child will grow to embody weapon or armor and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ayudhja belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Weapon or Armor.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ayudhja total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ayudhja" evokes a sense of strength, bravery, and protection. In Hindu mythology, Lord Ayudhya is the god of weapons, who is believed to protect and bestow the power of winning battles to his devotees. Thus, the name "Ayudhja" can be seen as a reminder of the importance of keeping one's weapons or tools ready to face the challenges of life. In Hindu communities, it is often given to babies as a mark of good luck, symbolizing the belief that they will be wardens of their families and bring victory in all their endeavors.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Ayudhja" holds a deeper spiritual significance as well, symbolizing the idea that one's possessions, be it material or spiritual, can be used as a means to protect and serve others. It is a reminder that the true purpose of acquiring material wealth, skills, knowledge, and even relationships, is to employ them for the betterment of oneself and others. The name "Ayudhja" thus represents the ongoing spiritual journey of an individual who seeks to use their God-given abilities to protect, serve, and uplift others, just as Lord Ayudhya protects and empowers his devotees.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ayudhja, meaning 'helper' or 'supporter', signifies the belief in the divine presence and assistance in times of need. It underlines the significance of unity and mutual support in personal and spiritual growth.

vedic_reference.note: Not found in Vedas or Upanishads.

historical_references.reference: The ancient Hindu kingdom of Ayudhya, also known as Sukhothai, was located in central Thailand. It was founded in 1238 AD by King Ramkhamhaeng, who is believed to have expanded the kingdom from the small town of Sukhothai to a powerful state that dominated much of northern and central Thailand.
historical_references.context: Founding of Ayudhya by King Ramkhamhaeng

historical_references.reference: Ayudhya was later the capital city of the Siamese Kingdom from 1469 to 1767 AD, during which time it became a prominent center of Southeast Asian culture and trade.
historical_references.context: Ayudhya as the capital city of the Siamese Kingdom

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Ayudhja' has modern context in three distinct platforms: technology, gaming, and education. In technology, Ayudhja is the name of an open-source software development framework for Android applications. In gaming, Ayudhja is the name of a popular character in the Indian mythological game 'Ayudhya: The Last Kingdom'. In education, Ayudhja is the name of a virtual learning platform designed to provide accessible education to students in rural areas of India.

name_in_real_life.story: Maya Ayudhja from Kathmandu, Nepal embodies the meaning of Ayudhja - "Weapon or Armor". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.
